# Edward

> An open-source AI assistant that remembers, notices what matters and works on your Mac, for one person. Next.js PWA, FastAPI, PostgreSQL with pgvector, LangGraph, and the Claude API for every model call. macOS on Apple silicon only. Apache-2.0.

Edward runs on the owner's own Mac and keeps everything he knows in their PostgreSQL database; the one outside service he needs is the Claude API. Every memory records who said it, what it is about and how sure he is. He answers in a chat PWA, by voice and in iMessage (@Edward in any chat), works in a sandboxed computer of his own (a persistent shell, a file editor and a headless browser: 14 tools on every surface), keeps his promises with scheduled follow-up wakes, writes a journal of what he does on his own, and stays inside a daily spend cap (default $5). Noticing what matters in the owner's messages is opt-in.

## Key facts

- Platform: macOS on Apple silicon only (not Intel, Linux, Windows or Docker)
- Model: the Claude API via one adapter, a route per purpose (Sonnet 5.5 for chat, wakes and screens; Haiku 5.5 for background memory work; Opus 5.5 for evaluations); an unofficial Codex fallback is opt-in
- Spend: a daily cap ($5 by default), $3 per turn the owner asked for, $1 per other turn
- Memory: pgvector (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dims, local) blended 70/30 with BM25; origin (heard, read, thought, did), about, tier and source on every row
- Tools: bash, str_replace_based_edit_tool, web_search, web_fetch, browser, chrome, look, messages, send_message, tell_owner, memory, schedule, screen, plan
- Off by default: reading messages and mail, noticing, Chrome hands, friends' full toolset, approvals, voice, push, the knowledge graph, the hub's pets
- Removed since March 2026: self-evolution, Lightpanda, the Python/JavaScript/SQL sandboxes, LangSmith, the morning briefing and its siblings; workers are dormant
